title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the combinatorics of the boundary of M_{g,ν}. A 'standard' curve X over an algebraically closed field k is a nodal curve with ν marked smooth points I (the 'points at infinity'). Y = X̃ is its normalisation, with components Y_α (α ∈ S, the vertices) of genus g_α. Ã is the set of oriented arcs (half-edges), i.e. the preimages of the double points. The previous page defines the total weight ν̂_α = ν_α + w_α, where ν_α = card I_α and w_α = card Ã_α is the order of the vertex. ν̂_α is the number of special points on Y_α.

This page finishes the list of equivalent definitions of a 'stable' curve:
(a) Aut X is finite.
(b) Every pointed component (Y_α, I_α ∪ Ã_α) is anabelian, i.e. 2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α > 0. Concretely: if g_α = 1 then ν̂_α ≥ 1, and if g_α = 0 then ν̂_α ≥ 3.
(c) Every vector field on Y vanishing on I ∪ Ã is zero, i.e. there are no infinitesimal automorphisms.
(d) The automorphism group scheme Aut(Y, Ã, I) is finite étale over k.

Form (b) depends only on the 'maquette' of X. The maquette is the combinatorial dual graph G = (S, Ã, σ) with genus function g: S → ℕ and leg set I.

Definitions:
- An MD-curve ('Mumford–Deligne', or 'modulaire') is a stable curve that is 0-connected (connected and non-empty).
- Their maquettes, the 0-connected stable maquettes, are called MD-graphs. These are exactly today's stable graphs (of type (g, n)), which index the strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,n}.

NB: a maquette is an MD-graph iff
(a) G is connected and non-empty;
(b) it is not a single genus-1 vertex with no edges and no legs;
(c) every genus-0 vertex has total weight ≥ 3.
This works because in a connected graph with ≥ 2 vertices every vertex has order ≥ 1, so the genus-1 condition can only fail for an isolated vertex.

The next page proves that an MD-graph has anabelian type: 2g + ν ≥ 3, where g = Σ g_α + h_1. This is the standard fact that stable graphs only exist for 2g − 2 + n > 0.
errors: No real errors. In (a), 'Aut X fini' should strictly be read as finiteness of the automorphism group scheme, or as finite plus unramified. Over an algebraically closed field the abstract group of k-points being finite is equivalent here, but (c) and (d) carry the infinitesimal content.
The genus-1 clause of the NB is equivalent to the vertex-wise condition only because the graph is connected. Grothendieck implicitly uses this, and it is correct.
Loops must be counted twice in ν̂_α. This is handled automatically because w_α counts oriented arcs (half-edges).

ideas.what: Equivalent characterisations of stability of a pointed nodal curve: finite Aut; each pointed normalised component has 2g−2+n>0; no nonzero vector fields vanishing at special points; finite étale automorphism scheme
ideas.modern_name: Deligne–Mumford(–Knudsen) stability of pointed nodal curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{g,ν}-bar and 'anabelian' (g,ν) but not this list

ideas.what: Combinatorial 'maquette' (dual graph with genus labels and legs) and the notion of an MD-graph = connected stable maquette
ideas.modern_name: stable graph of type (g,n) / dual graph of a stable curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore from Deligne–Mumford; formalised in Kontsevich–Manin (1994) and Getzler–Kapranov, Modular operads (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification of M_{g,ν}-bar by such combinatorial types, but MD-graph terminology is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Reading 'MD' as either 'Mumford–Deligne' or 'modulaire', and the term '0-connexe' for connected non-empty
ideas.modern_name: terminology; 'modular' graphs as in modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov for 'modular' in the operadic sense

missed.claim: Grothendieck coins 'MD-graphes' (MD = Mumford–Deligne or 'modulaire') for stable graphs. This anticipates the later 'modular' naming (modular operads, modular graphs) for exactly the same combinatorial objects. It is a terminological and historical priority note, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: On dit que X est une MD-courbe (MD, initiales de "Mumford-Deligne" — ou de "modulaire") si elle est stable, et 0-connexe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck systematically treating the boundary of M_{g,ν} via a category of stable graphs before the operadic literature. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: a careful restatement of Deligne–Mumford stability and the definition of stable graphs. The only mildly notable points are the private terminology ('maquette', 'MD-graphe' read as 'modulaire') and the date-uncertain anticipation of the stable-graph combinatorics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'on a ν̂_α ≥ 1' is correct. In line 2 the image reads 'on a' (abbreviated), not a dot.
In d), the image shows Aut(Y, Ã_K, I); the subscript is probably a sloppy indication, likely just Ã.
The struck-out character before 'I ∪ Ã' is a crossed-out letter (likely 'A'), not meaningful.
'maquette' readings are plausible and consistent across the page. The NB heading reads 'Une maquette est un MD-graphe ssi'.
In NB b): 'pas d'arête, pas de points marqués' — the image reads '(pas d'arête, pas de points marqués)', consistent with the transcription.
